dependency_stages.basis: Direct construction gives ratio R* as a lower example; no upper bound is assumed.
Universal kernel inequalities; this proof is independent of global attainment.
Fixed-template compactification at E=1 uses finitely many monomials.
Template stationarity, sampling, padding to 1/80, and standard cut compactness.
Globality justifies edge/profile variations; padding preserves the global ratio.
Moment/compression argument and the construction lower bound yield active density > p*.
Separate exact finite identities and spans; theorem truth is not assumed by their verification.
Pad the global maximum, apply the certificate and positive slope, compare with construction.
After the bound, equality kernels are global; zero squares imply triangle removal and the twin quotient.
Self-contained local Clebsch analysis, including the unnumbered fractional and variation arguments.
Peeling, positive-degree compactness, local defects and whole-vertex rounding.
Structural energy and integer class variance give the order of the edge deficit.
Clebsch profile geometry, its finite envelope, explicit constructions and the scalar profile optimization.
Structural reduction, profile optimization and the finite pair/template coefficients.
Finite integral mass deviations and pair errors yield the lattice correction and exact +/-1 cases.
Bounded defect data produce a finite polynomial list; this does not compute a global k_0(j).

dependency_scope: Selected mathematical implications, not an exhaustive graph; ordinary source citations are not converted into proof dependencies. Theorem 1.1/1.3 components are kept separate to avoid a spurious cycle.
limitations: This is a parser for the explicit source syntax of this manuscript, not a general TeX interpreter.
The inventory neither validates mathematical deductions nor turns a review status into a proof.
Literal named references are checked as navigation targets; bare numerical prose and all possible natural-language reference forms are not interpreted.
The absence of label-based reference commands is recorded explicitly; current named result references are literal text.
External citation arguments are excluded from internal result numbering checks.
A proof location records where an argument is supplied, not that the argument is correct.
